title: v3 payload descriptor
description: How the invoke payload for one call is transported. v1 and v2 inline the exported tree directly on the request body, which silently couples the maximum size of a plugin's input to whatever a single HTTP request can carry. v3 makes transport an explicit, closed choice instead: exactly one of an inline body or an out-of-band pull, discriminated by `mode`, with the same integrity metadata (media type, byte length, SHA-256 of the exact bytes) present either way so a plugin verifies what it received identically in both modes. The digest is computed over the exact UTF-8 bytes the host produced; a plugin MUST NOT re-serialize the parsed document and compare digests, because JSON serialization is not canonical. Making transport explicit is also what keeps it honest: a host MUST NOT switch a plugin to pull implicitly - the plugin has to advertise capabilities.payload_pull and negotiate contract_version 3 first, and a v1/v2 plugin that is handed too much data gets a clear failure rather than a payload shape it has never seen.

mediaType.description: Media type of the payload bytes. Fixed to application/json for this contract version; declaring it explicitly means a future binary payload form does not have to change the envelope's shape.
mediaType.$comment: The trailing negative lookahead is an ECMA-262-compatible exact end-of-input assertion.

sizeBytes.description: Exact length in bytes of the payload document, capped at 50 MiB. The cap is part of the contract rather than a deployment detail so that a plugin can size its own buffers from the schema alone.

mode.description: The payload document is carried directly in `data`.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 bytes of the payload document as the host serialized it.

data.description: The exported content tree itself. Present only in inline mode; a pull-mode descriptor never carries payload content, and this schema's closed-world definitions make the two mutually exclusive rather than merely conventionally so.

mode.description: The payload document must be fetched from `url`. No payload content appears anywhere in the invoke request.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact bytes the pull endpoint will return, known to the plugin before it fetches them, so a truncated or substituted response is detectable without trusting the transfer.

url.description: Absolute HTTPS URL of the host's payload endpoint for this invocation. The host supplies the complete URL so the plugin never constructs or guesses a host-side location (the same anti-SSRF reasoning as host_api_base_url). It always points at the host's own API; it is never a redirect to, or a pre-signed URL for, third-party object storage.

access_token.description: Short-lived Host Access Token authorizing exactly one payload read scope for exactly this invocation (see v3/host-access-token-claims.schema.json). It is a distinct token type from any user-facing token and is presented in addition to - never instead of - the HMAC signature required by the pull scheme in docs/security.md.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant after which the payload is no longer retrievable. A plugin that has not fetched by then must fail the invocation rather than retry indefinitely; the host is free to delete the bytes at that point.
